reason: Decides which criteria count toward the gate; changing it would alter missing-evidence detection and the completion status.
Defines what counts as satisfying a criterion; loosening it would let non-passing evidence mark criteria as covered.
Determines the no-gate-evidence state, which drives the partial status, the risk text and the summary.
Controls the early research-only status, which bypasses the blocked and failed classification.
Research-only takes precedence over blocked or failed evidence; reordering would change the reported status.
Any blocked evidence yields a blocked status.
When evidence is both blocked and failed, blocked is reported instead of failed.
Any failing evidence yields a failed status.
Failed evidence is reported before the disabled-policy partial status.
A disabled gate must never return verified; changing this check would affect that guarantee.
Without criteria or evidence the result must be partial, not verified.
Prevents a verified status when no applicable criteria exist.
This is the sole gate to a verified status; weakening it would verify incomplete work.
Not-applicable criteria keep their status instead of being reclassified.
Decides whether each criterion is reported as verified or unverified.
Controls whether residual risks from passing evidence appear in the unresolved risks.
Selects the disabled-gate risk message over the generic no-evidence messages.
Adds the risk that neither criteria nor evidence were provided.
Adds the risk that no acceptance criteria were provided.
Failed checks are recorded in the unresolved risks returned to the caller.
Blocked checks are recorded in the unresolved risks returned to the caller.
Not-run checks are recorded in the unresolved risks returned to the caller.
Chooses which missing-evidence detail appears in the summary.
Selects the verified summary text.
